summary: Minimal single-text-pane window initialiser: it runs the UI base initialiser and binds the text pane named 'txt' at the window's layout id through vtable slot +0x34; the owning screen is unknown.
evidence: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init 0x004AACC0 (still maybe_Ui_TextPane2_Init in the batch) is drN(self) followed by (**(code **)(*self+0x34))(self,0x4AAD00 /*'txt'*/, (u32)*(u16*)(self+0x28)<<16, 0); a lone 'txt' pane does not identify the screen. 0x004AAD04 right after it is the trivial deleting destructor (Ui_Object_DtorBase 0x001A6768 + free 0x0010F6CC), so this is a small Ui_Object-family text widget, not a full window. The 212-byte batch size is only max_strong_field+width and comes from the phantom 0xD0 access below; sibling S_141 class Ui_TextPane (0x00478970) has the identical body. The real text-layer key field is the u16 at +0x28 (ldrh r1,[r4,#0x28]), not part of this batch.

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: No real field: 0xD0 = 4 x vtable slot 0x34 ('(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))(param_1,0x4aad00,...)'). The disassembly of 0x004AACC0 reads only [r4] (vtable), [r4,#0x28] and [r2,#0x34] (slot) - it never touches self+0xD0; struct_db scaled the virtual pane-bind slot by the pointer width.

summary: Two-pane level-1 text row window (class vtable 0x007780A8): its initialiser binds the 'txt_l1' pane and a second 'txt_l2' pane through vtable +0x34, and its visibility override forwards to the animated pane setter.
evidence: The class constructor is 0x004C6228 (immediately after the two pane-name literals): it calls Ui_Object_CtorBase 0x001A66A0, stores vtable 0x007780A8 at +0 and clears byte +0x49. Slot 8 of that vtable is maybe_Ui_TextRowL1_Alt_Init 0x004C61AC, which binds s_txt_l1 (0x004C6218) and the second id 0x004C6220 ('txt_l2') with node ids (u16 self+0x28)<<16 and |1; slot 7 is the SetVisible override 0x004C6178 (Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim). The third batch function 0x004EE838 (now Ui_TxtL1Window_Init) binds only 'txt_l1' and is a sibling window merged under this generated class name. 212 is likewise a lower bound; the real layout is the Ui_Object base plus the pane/cursor members of drN (0x001A6520).

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: No real field: 0xD0 = 4 x vtable slot 0x34 ('ldr ip,[r2,#0x34] ... blx ip' in 0x004C61AC, and the bare '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))' in the other functions). Both constructors only read [r4,#0x28] (u16 layout id) and [r4] (vtable); nothing accesses self+0xD0.

summary: Two-value text row of the battle spell window: it formats two integers and writes them as the text of child text layers 1 and 2 of its layout node ((f_28<<16)|1 and |2).
evidence: Ui_TextRows_SetFormattedValues 0x004EE8E8 (only batch method) formats both arguments with func_006F0F1C and calls func_001A6680 (Ui_TextLayer_SetText) with node ids ((u32)f_28<<16)|1 and |2. Its caller Ui_BattleSpellWindow_Refresh 0x00391118 passes the battle index/count pair, and the self pointer is handed to the text-layer API as a widget, so the recovered UiWidget base fits; no base-ctor call is in the batch. 44 is only max_strong_field+width - the real object is a full Ui_Widget/window-sized row.

fields.name: textLayerId
fields.evidence: Read twice as self->f_28: Ui_TextRows_SetFormattedValues builds the child node ids (u32)self->f_28<<16 | 1 and | 2 for Ui_TextLayer_SetText. The same u16-at-+0x28 text-layer key is used by Ui_TextRow_SetSpellText 0x0045FFA8 ((u32)f_28<<16 root id), Ui_DirectionIndicator (S_137, named textLayerId) and Ui_TextBlink.

summary: Eight-byte intrusive list node used by Ui_UpdateInput's touch-focus pass: word +0 is the candidate UI object (vtable class tag 0x7C3330) and +4 links to the next node.
evidence: maybe_Ui_TouchFocus_FlagOverlap 0x006E30F0 (caller Ui_UpdateInput 0x0015FB70) iterates 'do { puVar10 = *begin; ... begin = (int*)begin[1]; } while (*begin != *end)'. Each node's word +0 is dereferenced as a UI object of class tag 0x7C3330 whose +0xB8 render child, +0x128 layer byte and +0x124..+0x127 rectangle are tested; the batch class name comes from this function, so the recovered object is the list node, not the focused widget.

fields.name: next
fields.evidence: 'begin = (int *)begin[1]' at the end of the do-loop walks the list by the node word at +4, and the loop ends when *begin == *end; the node is 8 bytes, +0 holding the tested UI object and +4 the forward link.

summary: Two-pane animation block: the anim-ref at +0 plays 'bottom_in' and the second anim-ref at +0x50 plays 'bottom_out' for the bottom pane of a two-pane window.
evidence: Ui_TwoPane_PlayBottomAnims 0x002D9954 calls Ui_AnimRef_Bind(self,animArg,s_bottom_in,0) and Ui_AnimRef_Bind(self+0x50,animArg,s_bottom_out,0), then Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame(self)/func_003E043C(self,0) and the same pair on self+0x50. The two anim-refs are embedded (their addresses are passed, not loaded), so 84 = 0x50+4 only covers the head of the second one. structs.json Ui_TimerDisplay shows the same +0x50 Ui_AnimRef pattern (six panes at +0x50..+0x35C, stride 0x9C).

fields.name: bottomAnim
fields.evidence: self+0x50 is passed to Ui_AnimRef_Bind(...,'bottom_out') and to Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame/func_003E043C as a Ui_AnimRef; the sibling ref at +0 is bound to 'bottom_in'. Embedded object; the 4-byte address width and Ui_AnimRef* type follow the batch and the S_139/S_015 precedent.

summary: Two-pane value label: pane 0 shows an optional icon from the widget icon map and pane 1 a number, used by the skill panel's required-SP display.
evidence: Ui_ValueLabel_SetNumberIcon 0x004DB120 and Ui_ValueLabel_SetNumberPair 0x004DB1A4, both called only from Ui_SkillPanel_UpdateRequiredSp 0x0036F2E0, format values with func_006F0F1C and write node ids (f_28<<16) and (f_28<<16)|1 through func_001A6680 (Ui_TextLayer_SetText); the icon variant first fetches widget-map entry 0xC with func_00641090. The recovered signatures take UiWidget* self, hence the Ui_Widget base. 44 is only max_strong_field+width.

fields.name: textLayerId
fields.evidence: Read four times as self->f_28: both setters address the two text layers by node id (u32)self->f_28<<16 and <<16|1. Same u16-at-+0x28 text-layer key as Ui_TextRows, Ui_TextRow_SetSpellText and S_137's Ui_DirectionIndicator (textLayerId).

summary: In-place constructor for a group of six 0x9C-byte parts after a vtable word - the same six-part, 0x9C-stride geometry as the six digit panes of the timer display; no caller, so the owning screen is unknown.
evidence: maybe_Ui_WindowWith6Blocks_Ctor 0x002BBA28 stores its first argument (the vtable) at +0 and calls std_ConstructArray(self+4, Ui_TimerDisplayPart_Ctor 0x00368118, 0x9C, 6). The twin Ui_TimerDisplay_InitDigitPanes 0x002BBA60 does exactly the same with literal vtable 0x0075F928 (and slot 0 of that vtable is 0x002BBA60 itself), and Ui_TimerDisplay_SetTimeFromCentiseconds 0x002BB90C drives six Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame calls at +0x50,+0xEC,+0x188,+0x224,+0x2C0,+0x35C (stride 0x9C). The written object is therefore 4+6*0x9C = 0x3AC bytes; the recorded size 4 is a lower bound.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*param_1 = param_2' at the top of the constructor, immediately before the six 0x9C parts are constructed at +4. The twin initialiser 0x002BBA60 stores the literal 0x0075F928 in the same slot, and index 0 of vtable 0x0075F928 is 0x002BBA60, so +0 is the vtable.
